methods.name: MCP statistics, hypothesis and time-series options: R and CLI spellings accepted, unknown values refused
methods.reference: the R functions each tool reproduces (power.t.test, power.prop.test, ks.test, t.test, mood.test, poisson.test, acf, Box.test, ar, decompose, runmed, filter, cpt.var, mad, cov.wt) at the option values R names
quantities: KS D, D+ and asymptotic p against punif(-1.5, 3) and pexp(0.8)
one-sided t, Mood and Poisson p
acf, acvf, pacf and the white-noise bound
methods.tolerance: validation/README.md by n (Tol::coef/se/stat/p_value); power 1e-10 relative (WP38's ports, <= 1.8e-14); printed values at their decimals (t-test 6, decompose and changepoint 4)

deviations.note: one-sample asymptotic p pinned; exact p not compared

methods.name: MCP timeseries_ccf: R's lag convention and lead/lag reading
methods.reference: stats::ccf(x, y, lag.max = 5): value at lag k = cor(x[t+k], y[t])
methods.tolerance: validation/README.md, n = 64: values 1e-5 relative, bound 1e-6, lags exact

methods.name: MCP stats_spline: R's default n and the n field
methods.reference: stats::spline(method = 'natural'), n = 3 * length(x) and n = 1, on complete (x, y) pairs
quantities: x and y at the 30 default points

methods.name: MCP multivariate_factanal factor scores (Bartlett, regression) returned and stored
quantities: score columns of the output dataset
methods.tolerance: iterative: Tol::iterative(1e-4) (STAT-62's factanal rule); an R emulation of p2a's default fixed point gives 3.77e-5

methods.name: MCP power tools solved for any parameter; Mauchly against Sigma; loglin convergence notes
methods.reference: stats::power.t.test, power.prop.test, power.anova.test (uniroot default tol); mauchly.test(Sigma = diag(1:4)); loglin(no three-way interaction)
quantities: Mauchly W, chi2, df, p (second order), first-order p, GG epsilon with and without Sigma
loglin G2, X2, df, max_deviation, non-convergence warning
methods.tolerance: power 1e-10 and roots 1e-9 relative (WP38's ports reproduce R to <= 2.2e-14); validation/README.md for Mauchly (n = 15) and loglin (720 counts)

deviations.note: p_value is pinned to the Anderson second-order p (psi_contrasts_p_anderson, contrasts_p_anderson); R's mauchly.test p is a 1e-3 cross-check only

methods.name: MCP spectrum interval multipliers (none for AR) and the Mahalanobis threshold at the covariance rank
methods.reference: stats:::plot.spec spec.ci; stats::spec.ar (no df); stats::mahalanobis; qchisq(0.95, rank)
quantities: refusal of a singular covariance (rank 1 of 2)
methods.tolerance: multipliers 1e-10 relative (WP40); validation/README.md otherwise; distances at their 4 printed decimals

deviations.note: p2a 18 for spans c(3, 3), spec.pgram 6.552102376599634; multipliers pinned at p2a's df

methods.name: MCP VAR, impulse responses, Granger, VARMA and VECM results as JSON
methods.reference: vars::VAR, vars::irf, VARselect; lmtest::grangertest; Hannan-Rissanen written out (T3-WP13); urca::ca.jo, cajorls, vars::vec2var
quantities: VAR coefficients, SEs, t, p, Sigma_u, logLik, AIC, BIC, VARselect criteria
Granger F, p, df at order 2 and the capped default 6
VARMA coefficients, SEs, p, logLik, AIC, BIC at m = 8 and the default 35
VECM trace and max-eigen statistics, 5% critical values, eigenvalues, beta, alpha, Gamma, selected rank (const, none, longrun)
methods.tolerance: validation/README.md by n (VAR 82, Granger 20, VARMA 391/364, VECM 53)

methods.name: MCP GARCH (normal and Student-t, forecasts), Holt-Winters intervals, cpgram, StructTS BSM, CausalImpact notes
methods.reference: written-out GARCH(1,1) likelihood (T3-WP35); stats::HoltWinters + predict(prediction.interval = TRUE); the body of stats::cpgram; stats::StructTS(type = 'BSM') tight optimum
quantities: GARCH parameters, SEs, logLik, 10-step variance forecasts (norm, std)
cpgram band, Stephens statistic, p, maximum deviation, first 20 frequencies and ordinates
AR warnings key (mcp_series_t3), MBIC, cpgram and filter descriptions
methods.tolerance: GARCH parameters and forecasts 1e-8, SEs 1e-6 relative (WP35); Holt-Winters at 4 printed decimals; validation/README.md otherwise; StructTS Tol::iterative(1e-6) (WP36)

deviations.note: predict.HoltWinters' multiplicative interval formula is wrong; the tool prints point forecasts and a note for multiplicative fits, intervals only for additive and non-seasonal fits (hw_add_upr, hw_add_lwr pinned)

methods.name: MCP handler tests for the remaining statistics, hypothesis and time-series tools (STAT-46, STAT-77)
methods.reference: TukeyHSD, pairwise.wilcox.test, wilcox.test, mcnemar.test, poisson.test, model.tables, se.contrast, cor, cancor, quantile(type = 6), PP.test internals, Box.test, decompose, ar(burg), runmed, embed, window, filter, diffinv, toeplitz, ARMAtoMA, acf2AR, ARMAacf
quantities: see validation/stats/mcp_stats_ts.md, one row per test
methods.tolerance: validation/README.md by n; printed values at their decimals; counts exact

deviations.note: one-sided p and the rate-ratio estimate pinned; the one-sided intervals are not (the tool returns the two-sided interval for every alternative, a core observation recorded in the method document)
p2a reports R1; R's W pinned through W = R1 - n1(n1 + 1)/2
means, grand mean and group sizes pinned
the tool returns x[t + k]; R's dplyr-style lag is lag_dplyr3_head
constant pinned here (keep in the option test); R's median is runmed_median_head
